newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Lebed snubs new defence council.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Lebed snubs new defence council.

text.p: Russia's controversial security chief Alexander Lebed ignored the first meeting of the Defence Council on Friday in a clear sign of dissatisfaction with the new grouping and his role within it.
"He is working on the documents signed yesterday," a Lebed spokesman said by telephone, referring to deals signed on Thursday with separatist leaders of Chechnya.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin chaired the meeting on behalf of President Boris Yeltsin. Government ministers and army and security bosses all attended.
Russian news agencies said the meeting, held behind closed doors, discussed funding for the armed forces -- an issue over which Lebed campaigned publically over the last few weeks.

Last month Lebed, in his capacity as the secretary of the Security Council, wrote a strongly-worded letter to Chernomyrdin saying the 1997 budget should be revised to grant more money to the army to salvage it from collapse.
He warned, in a newspaper interview, that delays in payments to servicemen could lead to mutiny.
But Interfax news agency said there were serious differences of opinion at Friday's meeting.

The military complained bitterly that lack of money was undermining Russia's military capabilities. "A real danger has emerged of damaging the military and technical ability which had been achieved through colossal effort," Interfax said.
Government representatives said the army was too big, with too many generals and too much bureaucracy.

"Participants reached the conclusion that serious reorganisation of the armed forces was needed which would take into consideration both the military and political state of the country and real economic conditions," Interfax said.
Yeltsin, in hospital preparing for heart surgery, in June appointed Lebed as his security adviser and secretary of the Security Council which groups top security and state officials.
The move followed Lebed's strong showing in the first round of the presidential election and aimed to boost Yeltsin's chances of winning the July 3 runoff.
But, in a clear sign that he was trying to curb Lebed's strive for power, Yeltsin set up the Defence Council in late July, making Lebed an ordinary member of the new body.
The president chairs the Defence Council, Chernomyrdin is his deputy and Yuri Baturin, formerly Yeltsin's security adviser is its secretary.

On Thursday, Lebed threatened to resign during a meeting with Yeltsin in the Central Clinical Hospital over a presidential decision to remove him as head of a committee on senior military appointments. Yeltsin gave the post to Baturin.
The president told Lebed to stay and urged him to work more closely with the government of Chernomyrdin, to whom he had delegated some of his own powers while he stays in hospital.
Chernomyrdin is constitutionally number two in Russia but Lebed has made little secret of presidential ambitions.
